messages:
anya: trying to enable fp8 kernel on L40S for atlas7b-v2. H100 path looks fine, but on L40S our eval shows a small accuracy shift + occasional NaNs in logits. has anyone seen saturation/scale mismatch between compiler kernels and our quant path?

sam: can you paste the runtime flags and a short eval diff? even small perplexity/mrr jumps matter. also which quantizer are you using (gptq / awq)?

anya: using AWQ -> perchannel int8-like backend then fp8 runtime enabled on L40S. quick config we used:

```yaml
model: atlas7b-v2
runtime:
  enable_fp8: true
  kernel_variant: l40s-v2
  activation_clip: 16.0
  bias_scale_sync: false
  quant_path: awq
  trace_activations: false
```

sam: thanks. what's the eval diff? can you paste the top-level delta numbers (mrr/ppl/top1) for the canary vs baseline?

anya: small paste: "baseline (fp16 @ h100): mrr=0.421, ppl=12.3; fp8 @ h100: mrr=0.418 (ok); fp8 @ l40s: mrr=0.408, ppl=13.1". also saw a couple NaNs in logits.log around step 1234 :face_with_thermometer:.

kevin: we've hit a similar pattern. often it's activation scaling mismatch — compiler kernel uses a different post-gemm rescale than the quantizer expects. try forcing bias sync + lower clip: `activation_clip=8.0` and `bias_scale_sync=true`. also enable `quant_rescale_post_gemm=true` if supported.

anya: tried `activation_clip=8.0` + `bias_scale_sync=true` — NaNs dropped but accuracy still ~+3% mrr regression vs h100 fp16. so clip helps but doesn't close the gap.

oliver: can you run with traces on a failing batch? `--trace-activations --trace-layers top3` and share max per-layer activations. last time we saw max_act ~1.2e4 on L40S which overflowed fp8 exponent range.

anya: running that now, here's a trimmed log from the failing batch:

```
[trace] layer_17 max_act=1.23e4  -> exp_overflow_detected=true
[trace] layer_18 max_act=7.9e3
[warn] fp8_cast overflow at layer_17, replaced with NaN in logits for 2 tokens
```

ci-bot: canary 2301122400 failed: canary-fp8-l40s-atlas7b-v2 exit_code=137, region=us-west-2, run_id=canary-2301122400

sam: if overflow is the source, a pragmatic path is per-request / per-layer fallback routing: if any layer max_act > 4e3, route that request to int8 or fp16 path on L40S. we have a smart-router flag for this: `router.fallback_on_activation_threshold=4000`. also try `quant_rescale_post_gemm=true` as kevin said.

kevin: operational thresholds we've used: — if MRR_delta > 1% OR token_loglik_shift > 0.005 then route to int8 for that model variant. for per-layer routing, threshold = 4k is conservative but avoided false positives. we also incrementally lower clip until eval delta stabilizes.

anya: ack. i'll run a canary with `bias_scale_sync=true`, `quant_rescale_post_gemm=true` and router threshold 4k, and post the canary metrics. if that doesn't hit parity, we'll pin atlas7b-v2 fp8 to H100 only and keep L40S on int8 for now.

deploy-bot: rollback: fp8 rollout for atlas7b-v2 -> 0% in us-west-2 (triggered by canary fail). :arrow_backward:

sam: also add a short perf test: compare latency/cost delta between int8 fallback and fp8 when clipping is low — sometimes int8 ends up cheaper once you account for extra retries.

anya: will do. thanks all — posting results in this thread in ~30m.
